chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Shu'ayb al-Haddad from Bashshar ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّسِيئَةِ: Credit / deferred payment / selling on delay

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods for cash versus credit in Shia jurisprudence according to Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* serves as a cross-reference within the chapter on sales (*al-Bay'*), specifically addressing the distinction between cash (*naqd*) and credit (*nasi'ah*) transactions. By stating 'Like it' (*mithluhu*), it affirms the continuity of the preceding ruling, likely reinforcing the permissibility of deferred payment sales while cautioning against the specific prohibition of *nasi'ah* (deferred payment for deferred delivery) prevalent in pre-Islamic times. This brevity highlights the rigorous chain of transmission (*isnad*) characteristic of Shia hadith literature, where scholarly precision often favors direct linkage to established precedents.
